cards.name: Legal Department
cards.flavor: You'll be hearing from us. Repeatedly. At your home address.
cards.notes: Litigious (Pokémon's Rocky Helmet): a creature that attacks it takes 2 damage. A wall that sues.
cards.picture: A phalanx of identical lawyers in grey suits behind a long desk, each holding up a thick folder like a riot shield, a fist that punched the desk recoiling with a CEASE AND DESIST stapled to it.

cards.name: Job Rotation
cards.flavor: Everyone will now be doing someone else's job, badly. It builds character.
cards.notes: Skill Swap: target creature and the creature facing it swap abilities, for the combat. Their Signal Jammer on your Bodyguard's side of the table, and the other way round.
cards.picture: An office where the surgeon in scrubs is fixing the printer, the IT guy in a hoodie is holding a scalpel over a patient, and the HR woman is piloting a forklift through the open-plan floor, an EMPLOYEE ROTATION WEEK banner above them.

cards.name: Resignation Letter
cards.flavor: I quit. Effective immediately. Also I took the client list.
cards.notes: Memento: your weakest creature is sacrificed (an additional cost), and target enemy creature gets -3 Attack until it leaves play. Its exit takes the wind out of them.
cards.picture: A man walking out of a glass tower with a cardboard box of his things and a huge grin, a letter fluttering behind him, while through the window his former boss sits slumped at a desk buried under the work he left.

cards.name: Teflon Don
cards.flavor: Charged forty times. Convicted of being fabulous.
cards.notes: Teflon (Pokémon's Good as Gold): enemy statuses don't land on it. Every Mafia theme is Corporate: legality is a business with a high entry price.
cards.picture: A silver-haired mob boss in a camel coat and pinstripes strolling out of a courthouse waving to cameras, indictment papers sliding off his coat like water off a non-stick pan, two lawyers scooping them up behind him.

cards.name: Insurance Policy
cards.flavor: In the event of death, the beneficiary receives the killer.
cards.notes: Destiny Bond: Mutually Assured for 3 Days on target friendly creature: the creature that kills it is destroyed too. The policy pays out in kind.
cards.picture: An insurance agent in a beige suit sliding a policy across the desk to a nervous creature, the fine print magnified under a glass reading WHOEVER KILLS YOU, WE KILL, a tiny coffin-shaped paperweight on the desk.

cards.name: Seniority Priority
cards.flavor: The slowest to adapt go first. It's called experience.
cards.notes: Trend for 3 Days (Trick Room, Corporate's flavour): Rush Hour, the slowest act first.
cards.picture: A boardroom where a very old executive with a walking frame is being ushered to the head of the table past a queue of young employees frozen mid-stride, a plaque on the wall reading 40 YEARS OF SERVICE.

cards.name: DMCA
cards.flavor: This creature has been claimed by its rights holder. Your appeal has been automatically denied.
cards.notes: Imprison (the user, 2026-10-17): target enemy creature is destroyed (taken down), and for 2 Days the enemy can't play a card that shares its name with a creature on the board, either side's (every deck runs two copies: the second waits while a copy stands).
cards.picture: A lawyer in a sharp suit slapping a huge red COPYRIGHT STRIKE sticker over the face of a creature on a giant video thumbnail, a second identical thumbnail beside it greyed out with CLAIMED across it, a tiny APPEAL button crossed out.

cards.name: 3rd Parallel Job
cards.flavor: Sleep is for people with one income.
cards.notes: Belly Drum (the user, 2026-10-17): target friendly creature loses half its Health and its Attack doubles. The hustle: its Health for a monster.
cards.picture: A hollow-eyed man at three desks pushed together, a laptop and a different lanyard on each, three video calls on mute, an IV drip of coffee into his arm, the wall clock at 3:00, his biceps absurdly huge from typing.

cards.name: Overtime
cards.flavor: Just this once. Every week.
cards.notes: The user, 2026-10-16: a creature still deploying of yours comes in up to 2 Days sooner, and pays for it with Burnout: it's destroyed at the end of the first Day it's ready, so it gets that one Day to act. A Cleanse saves it. Corporate's tempo: a big body now, for one Day.
cards.picture: An office worker at a desk late at night, surrounded by empty coffee cups and energy drink cans, typing furiously with smoke rising from the keyboard, eyes bloodshot and wide open, a wall clock showing 3 a.m. and a calendar with every weekend crossed out.

cards.name: Peace the Frontier
cards.flavor: Please, regulate us. Only us can afford it. Also, could someone lend us a few billion?
cards.notes: The user, 2026-10-16: frontier AI labs lobbying the government for rules strict enough that no newcomer can compete, while they burn through cash and play the victim. Regulatory capture: every enemy creature still deploying waits 1 more Day; the lobbying isn't free, you take 2 damage.
cards.picture: Two tech executives in hoodies at a congressional hearing table, one tearfully holding up a sign reading REGULATE US (ONLY), the other quietly sliding a rulebook titled BARRIERS TO ENTRY across to a smiling senator, a burning pile of cash under the table.

cards.name: Casino
cards.flavor: The house always wins. Except the houses he owned.
cards.notes: A Trend for 3 Days: each Dawn the house's wheel spins the Day's weather for both sides (Heatwave, Rain, Hail, Tailwind, Rush Hour, Windfall), like the weather in a Pokemon battle. Corporate bets on tempo: whoever adapts best to the Day wins.
cards.picture: A caricature of Donald Trump in a dark suit and an overlong red tie, his blond hair swept over, grinning and throwing a fistful of casino chips in the air, in front of his gaudy gold-and-purple casino with onion domes and a giant neon sign, a red BANKRUPT stamp across the sign.

cards.name: Headhunter
cards.flavor: We found you on LinkedIn. We found everyone on LinkedIn.
cards.notes: Corporate's recruiting: Discard 1, then send for a creature from your deck; it joins your next hand.
cards.picture: A slick recruiter in a sharp suit reeling in a startled employee from a rival's office tower with a fishing rod baited with a stock-options contract.

cards.name: Counterfeit
cards.flavor: Genuine replica. 100% authentic copy.
cards.notes: Mechanics test: Wannabe (Active, hold Shift as you drag it onto a creature): its Attack, Health and Speed become that creature's.
cards.picture: A knockoff superhero in a cheap costume with a misspelled logo on the chest, flexing proudly in front of a mirror that shows a real muscled hero.

cards.name: Private Equity
cards.flavor: We don't buy companies. We buy what they used to be worth.
cards.notes: Mechanics test: Credit Grab (Active, once per combat): steals target creature's stat raises. Buff an enemy, or let them, then take it.
cards.picture: A vampire banker in a pinstripe suit sucking gold coins out of a little family shop through a long straw.

cards.name: Shell Company
cards.flavor: Registered in four countries. Exists in none.
cards.notes: Mechanics test: Shell Game (Active, hold Shift as you drag it onto a creature): that creature trades places with the one to its right. Moves an enemy into a planned attack, or out of the way of one.
cards.picture: A street hustler playing the shell game with three walnut shells, each stamped with a different tax haven's flag, a gold coin under one.

cards.name: Golden Parachute
cards.flavor: Ousted with a forty-million bonus. Failing upward, gently.
cards.notes: Replaced (the user, 2026-10-15: a new trigger, being replaced isn't dying): when a summon takes its slot, you draw 2. The executive leaves with the payout; send in the next one.
cards.picture: A grinning CEO floating down on a golden parachute stitched from banknotes, a briefcase overflowing with cash in hand, while the company tower he leaves behind burns and the staff watch from the windows.

cards.name: Work Shift Rotation
cards.flavor: Same job, new face. The vest is still warm.
cards.notes: Handover: when a summon replaces it, the newcomer takes over its stat changes and statuses. Buff it, then send in the next shift.
cards.picture: Two warehouse workers at the clocking-in machine: the exhausted one hands his hi-vis vest, still warm, to the fresh one.

cards.name: Unpaid Intern
cards.flavor: Paid in experience. The experience is this.
cards.notes: Future: a Worker token created by other cards rather than drafted. Fodder for sacrifice costs.

cards.name: Inhuman Resources
cards.flavor: We're here for you. "You" meaning the company.
cards.notes: Future: Layoffs. Destroy a friendly Worker as an additional cost; schedule 2 draws.

cards.name: Micromanager
cards.flavor: Per my last email. And the one before. And the meeting about the emails.
cards.notes: Future: gives a friendly Worker Coffeinated instead of a plain attack buff.

cards.name: Multilevel Marketing Seller
cards.flavor: It's not a pyramid. It's a triangle of opportunity.
cards.notes: Future: summons an Unpaid Intern token. Each recruit pays a share of its draws upward.

cards.name: Day Trader
cards.flavor: Time is money, friend. Up 300% by noon, rent due at five.
cards.notes: Insider Job (insider trading): its damage ignores Armor. Future: Investment. Pays out or loses cards depending on the Day.

cards.name: Pluriemployed Hustler
cards.flavor: Three jobs, two side hustles, one kidney left.
cards.notes: Penny Stock: small bets that pay double, so hits of 3 or less are doubled. Future: Coffeinated, then Burnout (the Hustle Culture pairing with Zeitgeist).

cards.name: Satoshi Nakamoto
cards.flavor: Mined a million coins. Never spent one. Never seen again.
cards.notes: Number go up: each Dawn, +1 Attack while it stays in play. Nobody knows who he is (Undercover: his plans show as ??? to the enemy). Starts harmless; leave him alone and he's a whale (the user, 2026-10-15).
cards.picture: A figure in a grey hoodie whose face is only a swirl of fog with a question mark in it, sitting cross-legged on a mountain of gold coins, a laptop glowing on his knees and a price chart behind him shooting straight up.

cards.name: Unicorn
cards.flavor: Valued at a billion. Burns a million a day. Profitable next year, every year.
cards.notes: Future: Unicorn (Enterprise) from the card examples. Burn rate stays: Corporate can't heal it.

cards.name: Multimillionaire Philanthropist
cards.flavor: Gave away 0.01% of his fortune. Wrote off 100% of it.
cards.notes: Future: a Contract. The enemy gets the gift now, you get the tax break on a later Day.

cards.name: Fat Tony
cards.flavor: Nothing personal. It's just business. Mostly the personal kind.
cards.notes: Future: An Offer You Can't Refuse. Recruits a damaged enemy creature instead of hurting it.

cards.name: Charles Ponzi
cards.flavor: Early investors were extremely satisfied.
cards.notes: Future: pays draws from your next Days until it collapses, then takes them all back.

cards.name: Margin Call
cards.flavor: Your position has been liquidated. Everyone's has. Have a nice day.
cards.notes: Prophecy 1-3 (the user, 2026-10-15): it comes in 1 to 3 Days, nobody knows which. Future: Capital cost, discard your hand; each creature takes damage equal to the cards discarded.

cards.name: Hostile Takeover
cards.flavor: We're not buying your company. We're buying its funeral.
cards.notes: Future: Capital cost, discard 2 cards. Placeholder cost: the enemy draws a card.

cards.name: Mass Layoffs
cards.flavor: We were never a family. Please return your badge.
cards.notes: Future: as an additional cost, destroy any number of your Workers; draw 1 per Worker next Day.

cards.name: Team Building Exercise
cards.flavor: Attendance is voluntary. Attendance is tracked.
cards.notes: Target side, yours or theirs (the user, 2026-10-15): every creature there takes 1 damage and gets +1 Attack. Everyone goes, management included. Future: Coffeinated, followed by Burnout.

cards.name: Dead Cat Bounce
cards.flavor: It's recovering! It's recovering! It's... no.
cards.notes: Target creature, either side (the user, 2026-10-15): it heals 2 now, the bounce, and takes 5 damage at the next Dawn, the crash.

cards.name: Business Expense
cards.flavor: The yacht was a business expense. So was the lawyer. So is the appeal.
cards.notes: Draw 2 next Day, and pay the fine now: 2 damage to you. Future: Capital cost, discard a card instead.
cards.picture: A CEO in a full three-piece suit, briefcase still in hand, being walked into a jail cell by a guard, while he hands the guard a receipt stamped BUSINESS EXPENSE.

cards.name: Business Operating Expenses
cards.flavor: Two years in a federal prison camp. Priced in. The stock went up.
cards.notes: Jail time as overhead (the user, 2026-10-15): target friendly creature goes dark until the next Dawn (it does its time) and you draw 2 next Day. Business Expense is the perks and the fine; this is the cell, written off.
cards.picture: A smiling executive in an orange jumpsuit with a silk tie, checking into a cushy white-collar prison camp with a tennis court and a golf green, an assistant wheeling his luggage behind him; a sign over the gate reads COST OF DOING BUSINESS.

cards.name: Taxpayer Funds Venture Capital Profits
cards.flavor: Privatize the gains. Socialize the bill.
cards.notes: The gains are yours alone: draw 2 with the next Day's hand. The bill is everyone's: 1 damage to every creature on the board, yours included.

cards.name: Cleaning Robot
cards.flavor: Cleans 30% of your floor. The other 70% is a Premium feature.
cards.notes: Mechanics test: a sturdy pusher. Pushing (every creature can), no chain pushes, blocked pushes ("needs Swap") and the automatic move order.
cards.picture: A smart-home robot vacuum in the style of a Google Nest (a soft fabric puck with four coloured light dots: blue, red, yellow, green), its single camera eye glowing, sucking up a family's photos, letters and diary from the living-room floor while a beam uploads a floor plan of the house to a cloud. A pop-up on it reads "Free cleaning. You're the product."

cards.name: Tax-Exempt Corruption
cards.flavor: Thou shalt not pay taxes.
cards.notes: Future: Capital cost (discard 2 cards). Placeholder cost: the enemy draws a card. Plays in Prosperity Gospel.
cards.picture: A megachurch whose cross is a giant gold dollar sign, a private jet parked by the door and a big red TAX EXEMPT stamp across the sky.

cards.name: Solidarity Towards The Small Businessman
cards.flavor: He's just a little guy. With seven yachts. Every coin helps.
cards.notes: Draw 2, paid for by your workers: 1 damage to each friendly creature. Future: Capital cost.
cards.picture: A fan-subscription website called ONLYFUNDS: the board-game tycoon (top hat, white moustache) poses in a pink bathrobe on a live webcam, a SUBSCRIBE button and a pile of tips beside him, while tired workers in hi-vis vests and scrubs send him their coins.

cards.name: Inheritance
cards.flavor: Self-made. Grandma did the making.
cards.notes: Old money: target friendly creature gets +2 Attack and +2 Health for good, for doing nothing. Future: when a friendly creature dies, another inherits its stats.
cards.picture: Grandma at peace in an open coffin, hands folded on lilies, while her grandson in his best suit grins over her, fanning out the banknotes from her will.

cards.name: NDA
cards.flavor: You saw nothing. You'll say nothing. Initial here, here and here.
cards.notes: Non-Disclosure Agreement. Discard 1 (Corporate pays with capital), then Blackout for 2 Days on target enemy creature: its ability and its effects (arrival, Dawn and Dusk, retaliation, Last Will) are switched off. Silences the Shadow Ops. tricks and the Myth sacrifices alike.
cards.picture: A smiling corporate lawyer holding out a gold pen to a nervous employee whose mouth is closed with a big brass zipper, a towering stack of contracts between them stamped CONFIDENTIAL.

cards.name: Inflation
cards.flavor: Same price. Less creature.
cards.notes: Everyone's money is worth less, theirs more so: 2 damage to every enemy creature and 1 to each of yours. Prophecy 2 (the user, 2026-10-15): it hits two Days later, as prices catch up.
cards.picture: A chocolate bar in its old-size wrapper, the bar inside visibly half as big, and a supermarket price tag re-stickered three times, each price higher.

cards.name: Escape Goat
cards.flavor: It wasn't us. It was the goat. Everyone agrees it was the goat.
cards.notes: Heat Signature 2 on target creature (random effects and redirected attacks go to it), and draw a card. Corporate since 2026-10-15 (the user): when something goes wrong, someone else takes the blame, and the damage finds the goat.
cards.picture: The escape goat: a white goat scrambling over a wooden fence, front legs over the top rail, looking back in a sweat.

cards.name: Laissez-Faire
cards.flavor: Let the market decide. The market decided: whoever already had the most.
cards.notes: Hands off: the strongest creature on the board, on either side, takes 1 Attack from every other creature. Nobody steers it, so play it when the biggest is yours. The Invisible Hand does the same, quietly, on your own side each Dusk.
cards.picture: A boxing referee lounging in a deck chair in the corner of the ring, reading the business pages, whistle unused, while a giant in a top hat sits on a heap of flattened small boxers and pockets their belts.

cards.name: The Invisible Hand
cards.flavor: Nobody has ever seen it. Everybody has felt it in their pocket.
cards.notes: Each Dusk your strongest creature takes 1 Attack from each of your other creatures, this one too: the market sorts itself out. Undercover: you never see it coming. Laissez-Faire does the same once, to the whole board.
cards.picture: An empty white glove floating over a busy market stall, nobody inside it, quietly lifting coins out of the shoppers' pockets and dropping them into a fat banker's top hat.

cards.name: C-Suite
cards.flavor: Record profits this quarter. The savings will trickle down to you shortly.
cards.notes: Collateral Damage (trample): when its attack is more than a creature's Health, the rest goes on to that creature's player. The top of Corporate's hierarchy; it costs capital: discard a card.
cards.picture: A champagne tower of glasses: five executives in suits at the top glass, toasting, the champagne overflowing past them down the tiers, until a line of workers at the bottom catch the last drips in paper cups.

cards.name: Venture Capital
cards.flavor: We're not investing in you. We're investing in your exit.
cards.notes: Persistent growth (Corporate's secondary): target creature +2 Attack/Health for good, and you draw 1 next Day.
cards.picture: A man in a fleece vest pouring a bucket of gold coins into a lanky startup founder's head through a funnel, the founder growing taller and more delusional.

cards.name: Corporate Bailouts
cards.flavor: Losses are public. Profits are private. Simple.
cards.notes: Discard 1 (Corporate's cost): Armor 3 on every friendly creature and you heal 3. Too big to fail.
cards.picture: A sinking cruise ship branded MEGABANK being lifted out of the sea by a giant hand made of taxpayers' wallets, the executives on deck popping champagne.

cards.name: Flash Crash
cards.flavor: Down 1,000 points in 36 minutes. The robots apologise.
cards.notes: Board damage (it wins 55%): 2 damage to every enemy creature. Discard 1. The 2010 crash.
cards.picture: A stock chart dropping off a cliff into a canyon, tiny traders in suits falling with it, a trading robot at the top shrugging.

cards.name: Just in Time
cards.flavor: Zero inventory. Zero slack. Zero idea what happens when the ship gets stuck.
cards.notes: Tempo (Corporate is a timing faction): target creature still deploying is ready 1 Day sooner, and you draw 1 next Day. Unlike Overtime it costs no Burnout.
cards.picture: A delivery van screeching up to a factory door exactly as the last box on the assembly line runs out, a manager holding a stopwatch at 0:00.

cards.name: Hedonic Treadmillionaire
cards.flavor: Third yacht. Still not happy. Buying a fourth.
cards.notes: A big body for a faction of small ones (Day Trader 3/1, Unpaid Intern 1/1): Arrival: you draw 1 next Day.
cards.picture: A billionaire in a gold tracksuit running on a treadmill that is itself on a yacht on a bigger yacht, sweating, his smile not moving.

cards.name: Moral Bankruptcy
cards.flavor: Ethics is a cost centre.
cards.notes: Removal: destroy target creature with 3 Attack or less. Corporate had damage but no clean kill.
cards.picture: A banker stamping BANKRUPT across a smiling worker's portrait, the worker's chair already being carried away by movers.

cards.name: Usury
cards.flavor: Interest on the interest on the interest. Compounded daily, forgiven never.
cards.notes: Ripening board damage: 1 to every enemy creature, 1 more for each Dawn it's kept in your hand (up to 4). Corporate's patience pays (Slay the Spire's Retain cards that grow).
cards.picture: A loan shark in a pinstripe suit feeding coins into a piggy bank swollen to the size of a house, a tiny debtor pinned under its trotter.

cards.name: Middle Manager
cards.flavor: Restructured. Again. Still somehow on the payroll.
cards.notes: Laid Off (creatures leave the hand at every Dawn now): when it's discarded from your hand, draw a card. Unplayed, it still pays; a discard cost paid with it costs nothing.
cards.picture: A middle manager carrying a cardboard box of desk things out of the office, a 'Synergy' mug on top, already on the phone to get rehired as a consultant.

cards.name: Big Four
cards.flavor: Four firms. Every audit. No findings.
cards.notes: Grudge (Kingambit's Supreme Overlord): +1 Attack for each friendly creature that died this combat, up to +5. The workers Corporate spends become its leader's raise.
cards.picture: Four identical accountants in grey suits shoulder to shoulder at a long table, the shredder behind them overflowing, a fifth chair empty with a name card reading 'Arthur Andersen'.

cards.name: Bloomberg Terminal
cards.flavor: Twenty-five grand a year to watch other people's money move.
cards.notes: On Trend (Protosynthesis): +2 Attack while a Trend is on. With Casino it rides the house's weather.
cards.picture: A black two-screen trading terminal with its keyboard of colored keys, every chart spiking green, a trader's sweaty finger hovering over the yellow BUY key.

cards.name: Internal Protocol: Quota Crusher Mindset
cards.flavor: Crush it. Then crush it again. The quota is a feeling.
cards.notes: Policy (Slay the Spire's Powers): your creatures +1 Attack this Day, and again at each Dawn, for the rest of the combat. An engine for Corporate's wide boards.
cards.picture: A motivational poster over a cubicle farm, a lone runner on a mountain top under the words QUOTA CRUSHER, the workers below asleep on their keyboards.

cards.name: High-Frequency Trading Scam
cards.flavor: Buy at a millisecond, sell at the next. Repeat until regulated. Nobody ever regulates.
cards.notes: Combo (Slay the Spire's Finisher): draw a card next Day, 1 more for each other spell you play this Day. Corporate's spells feed its draw.
cards.picture: A server rack in a basement next to the stock exchange, cables running under the street, a trader's face reflected in a screen of numbers moving too fast to read.

cards.name: Valet
cards.flavor: Premium parking, billed monthly. Your car has been moved for your convenience.
cards.notes: Logistics Maneuver: target friendly creature trades places with its partner in the formation (Flank with Flank, Headquarters with Headquarters, the Vanguard with the left Flank). A megacorp's valet subscription, moving your pieces.
cards.picture: A valet in a gold-trimmed uniform with a megacorp logo swapping two parked cars with a forklift, under a sign reading PREMIUM PARKING - SUBSCRIBERS ONLY.
